profileDefinition.general: A family that does not depend on an admin family. It may still implement workflows commonly used by admin applications.
profileDefinition.admin: A terminal family that may depend on general families and may never be imported by a general family.

nonFamilyExports.reason: Machine-readable profile metadata: every subpath available below the general dependency ceiling, and the optional peers that come with them. Data, not code — a tool asking what it may import needs a list rather than a paragraph.

The same for the admin ceiling, including the general families the two admin families reach down into. A record listing only the admin families would understate both the surface and the peers a consumer receives.
The processed global stylesheet's side-effect entry. Imported for what it emits, not for what it exports.
The complete catalogue — core plus every family, generated by concatenating the emitted sheets once each. The simplest installation.
Reset, tokens, themes and typography: the half every family depends on, and the sheet that declares the layer order. Imported first by every ESM entry, and by hand in a CJS consumer.

The Tailwind CSS v4 theme bridge: one `@theme inline` block mapping the token contract into Tailwind's namespaces. Not part of the cascade and never shipped as-is — a consumer imports it into their Tailwind entry, where it is read at build time and every key no utility uses is dropped. Generated from the tokens by scripts/gen-tailwind-bridge.mjs.

The token contract in W3C DTCG format, for Figma and design tooling. Data, not code: the runtime never reads it. Colours are OKLCH objects with a clipped `hex` fallback; `calc()` is resolved to a literal and the shadow ladder is absent, because DTCG has neither arithmetic nor `color-mix` — both stated in the file's own `$extensions`. Generated by scripts/gen-dtcg-tokens.mjs and checked by verify dtcg-tokens.
Individual token and theming sheets, so a consumer can take the contract without the components.
Conventional. Tooling reads it to resolve the package's own metadata.
